# Run agent sessions under limits and a schedule

## Intent

Every piece of work nightshift drives is done by agent sessions, and a
person who is not watching has to be able to trust what a session can
reach, what it may spend and when it runs. nightshift runs each session of
a planner, an implementer or a reviewer as a bounded process of an
operating-system user of its own, with a hub token that can only reach the
item's fork, records it on the hub and keeps its output; it starts
sessions in a fixed order under a limit of parallel sessions, a limit per
item and a daily token limit per workspace, asks the person when a step
keeps failing, and holds, resumes and survives a restart without losing an
item's place.

## Goals

- **A session cannot read nightshift's credentials or the person's
  files.** Sessions, and the gate and health commands that run the code
  they wrote, run as the operating-system user `[sessions].user` names; a
  daemon that cannot guarantee that does not start.
- **A reviewer with a fresh context.** Every review is a session of its
  own, on the configured provider and model, with a clone of its own and
  nothing of the writer's session.
- **Every session is on the hub's record.** It is registered with its
  role, model and item, its token usage is reported, and it ends
  `completed` or `failed`.
- **A session's token reaches the item's fork and nothing else**, and ends
  with the session.
- **A session is bounded.** One that writes nothing for 30 minutes, or
  uses 10,000,000 tokens, is ended.
- **A step that keeps failing reaches the person.** A failed session is
  tried once more; after the second failure in a row a `session_failed`
  decision asks.
- **One item cannot run without end.** After 12 implementer and reviewer
  sessions the item stops and a `session_limit` decision asks.
- **Independent items run at once, in a fixed order.** Up to 3 sessions
  run in parallel: repairs first, then items already `implementing` or
  `reviewing`, then `ready` items, oldest first.
- **Spending is bounded per workspace and day.** At the daily token limit
  no further session starts in the workspace until the next midnight.
- **The person can stop work without losing it.** An item or a whole
  workspace can be paused and resumed.
- **It survives a stop and a restart.** A session ended by a shutdown or
  lost in a crash is started again for the same step, and does not count
  as a failure.

## Non-goals

This package is the fourth of ten written from

## Background

Packages 01 to 03 leave a daemon with a store, an API, a hub client,
registered workspaces, work items in states and an inbox with decisions.
Nothing runs an agent yet. Every command, route, configuration key and Go
package this document names for sessions and scheduling is new:
`internal/session` and `internal/sched`.

What this package uses of Parley, as its `docs/api.md` states at commit
`7eabfb9`:

- A **session** is created with `POST /api/v1/sessions` (`workspace_slug`,
  an `id` the caller may choose, `archetype`, `model`, `metadata`), takes
  usage increments with `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/usage` (`model`,
  `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`) while it is
  `active`, and ends with `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/complete` (`status`
  `completed`, `failed` or `timeout`, `error_message`,
  `cache_creation_input_tokens`). A create with an `id` the caller already
  used answers `200` with the stored session, so it is safe to retry.
- A push names its session with the push option `parley.session=<id>`; the
  hub accepts a session of the workspace for work on a task fork of it.
- `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/tokens` mints a personal access token
  bound to a workspace or fork, with `permissions` and `expires` in days
  (`0`, `30`, `60` or `90`). A calling token can grant only scopes it
  holds **by exact name**: one that holds `git:write` cannot mint one with
  `git:read`. `DELETE /api/v1/user/tokens/{token_id}` revokes a token.
- Git authenticates with HTTP Basic, the token as the password; `git:read`
  fetches and `git:write` fetches and pushes.

`claude -p` is started as `specrun` of `agent-fox-dev/spec` starts it
(`docs/specrun.md` at commit `e9081fa`): `--output-format stream-json
--verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions --disallowedTools
ScheduleWakeup,CronCreate`, with `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`
set to the stall time; the last event of type `result` carries `is_error`.
`agentkit-go` v0.11.0 runs the reviewer: an `Agent` built from a `Config`
with a provider (`anthropic`, `openrouter` or `ollama`) and a model, whose
`Stream` yields the run's events and whose usage is a `core.Usage`.

## Requirements

Constraint: Linux and macOS; Windows is best effort. Constraint: `sudo` is
installed where a session user is configured, and the daemon's user may
run commands as the session user without a password (`sudo -n`).

### Configuration

This package adds these keys to the configuration file:

| Key | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[roles.planner].model` | the model the planner's `claude -p` runs | none, required |
| `[roles.implementer].model` | the model the implementer's `claude -p` runs | none, required |
| `[roles.reviewer].provider` | the `agentkit-go` provider of the reviewer | none, required |
| `[roles.reviewer].model` | the reviewer's model: a model id or a tier name | none, required |
| `[sessions].user` | the operating-system user sessions run as | none |
| `[sessions].unisolated` | `true`: run sessions as the daemon's user | `false` |
| `[sessions].dir` | where the items' clones and session files are kept | `nightshift` in the session user's home directory; `~/.nightshift/work` when unisolated |
| `[sessions].stall` | how long a session may write nothing | `30m` |
| `[sessions].max_tokens` | the tokens one session may use | `10000000` |
| `[sessions].max_parallel` | the sessions that run at once, 1 to 16 | `3` |
| `[items].max_sessions` | the implementer and reviewer sessions of one item between two answers of the person, 2 to 100 | `12` |
| `[limits].daily_tokens` | the daily token limit a workspace gets at registration | `50000000` |

A `max_parallel` outside 1 to 16, a `max_sessions` outside 2 to 100, or a
`stall`, `max_tokens` or `daily_tokens` that is not greater than zero fails
the start check `config` (`config: sessions.max_parallel must be between 1
and 16`, `config: sessions.stall must be greater than 0`).

### Roles and sessions

The configuration names three roles. `planner` and `implementer` each name
a model run by the Claude Code command (`claude -p`); `reviewer` names a
provider and a model run through `agentkit-go`. The provider and the model
may be the same as the planner's or the implementer's, or others. A role
that names no model, or a reviewer that names no provider or one
`agentkit-go` does not know, is invalid: the daemon does not start. The
start check `roles` runs after `credentials` and fails with `roles:
<role> names no model` (the first of planner, implementer, reviewer),
`roles: reviewer names no provider` or `roles: unknown provider "<name>"`.

**The reviewer's context is fresh.** Every review is a session of its own.
It starts with nothing of the planner's or the implementer's session: not
its conversation, not its reasoning, not its working directory. It is given
only what the package that starts it names as its input, and reads the
repository through a clone of its own. A later review of the same item
starts fresh too.

Every agent session is registered on the hub as a session on the item's
workspace with its role as `archetype`, its model, and the item's number in
`metadata`; the item's pushes name it. nightshift reports each session's
token usage to the hub when the session ends, and marks it completed or
failed.

A session is a process on the daemon's machine, in a clone of the item's
fork. The clone is kept between the sessions of one item and removed when
the item is `done` or `abandoned`.

Every agent session gets a token of its own, minted by nightshift, bound to
the item's task fork and holding `git:write` only (the reviewer's:
`git:read`). It expires with the session. Such a token can fetch and push
in its fork and can do nothing to a change: not open, land, abandon or edit
one.

**The session user.** Sessions run as the operating-system user
`[sessions].user` names, not as the daemon's user. So do the gate and the
health command, which run code a session wrote. The clones belong to that
user. The start check `sessions` runs after `roles` and fails, with these
reasons, when the key is missing (`sessions: no user configured; set
[sessions].user or [sessions].unisolated`), when the user does not exist
or is the daemon's own (`sessions: user "<name>" does not exist`,
`sessions: user "<name>" is the daemon's user`), when the daemon cannot
start a process as that user (`sessions: cannot run as "<name>":
<error>`), when that user can read the configuration file, the client
token or the daemon's store (`sessions: user "<name>" can read <path>`),
or when `claude` does not run as that user (`sessions: claude is not
available to "<name>": <error>`).

With `[sessions].unisolated = true` and no user, sessions run as the
daemon's user. The daemon then prints `warning: sessions run as the
daemon's user and can read its credentials` at start, and `status` reports
`sessions: unisolated`.

**What a session is given, and what it must leave.** A package that needs
a session gives the role, the item, the step the session is for, the fork,
the branch to work on (a planner or an implementer) or the commit to read
(a reviewer), a prompt, input files, and optionally a function that accepts
or refuses the result.

- A **planner or implementer** session is `claude -p "<prompt>" --model
  <the role's model>` with the flags above, run in the item's clone. In
  the prompt, `{result}` stands for the path of the session's result file
  and `{input:<name>}` for the path of an input file. The session must
  leave a result file that is one JSON document (the convention of PRD 09
  of `agent-fox-dev/spec`).
- A **reviewer** session is an `agentkit-go` agent on the role's provider
  and model with the file navigation tools over its own clone and no shell
  tool, given the prompt as its only message. Its last message must hold
  its verdict as one JSON object: `{"verdict": "agree" | "object",
  "findings": [{"text", "file"?, "line"?, "criterion"?}]}`, with at least
  one finding for `object`.

A session is ended and counts as failed:

- when it writes nothing to its output for `[sessions].stall` (30 minutes
  unless configured), with the reason `stalled`;
- when its input and output tokens, cache reads excluded, reach
  `[sessions].max_tokens` (10,000,000 unless configured), with the reason
  `token limit`.

A session that ends without the result its step requires, or with an
error, counts as failed with that error's first line (`no result` for a
missing or unreadable result file, `no verdict` for a reviewer's last
message without one). After a failed session the step is started once
more. After the second failure in a row for the same step, the item waits
on a decision of kind `session_failed`, showing both reasons and the path
of each session's stream; its options are `retry` and `abandon` (package
09 adds `take_over`).

**The limit per item.** nightshift counts the implementer and reviewer
sessions started for an item since it became `ready`, or since the person
last answered a decision of that item, whichever is later. When the count
reaches `[items].max_sessions` (12 unless configured, 2 to 100), no further
session starts for the item and it waits on a decision of kind
`session_limit`, showing each session with its role, its outcome and its
tokens; its options are `continue` (the count starts again) and `abandon`
(package 09 adds `take_over`).

The full output stream of every session is kept on the daemon's machine for
30 days and can be read with `nightshift session log <session-id>`.

### Scheduling and the daily limit

At most `[sessions].max_parallel` sessions (3 unless configured, 1 to 16)
run at once, over all workspaces. When more items could start than
sessions are free, they start in this order: repairs first, then items
already `implementing` or `reviewing`, then `ready` items by the time they
became `ready`, oldest first.

The scheduler drives every item: a package registers, for an item state,
the function that carries out that state's step, and the scheduler calls
it for each item in that state that is not paused and waits on no
decision, one call at a time per item, again after it returned. A step
that needs a session asks the scheduler for it and waits for its turn. A
package can also register a start guard: while a guard refuses an item, no
session starts for it, and the scheduler reports the guard's reason as what
the item waits for.

While the hub is unreachable, or the worker token is not accepted, no
session is started; running sessions go on.

**The daily limit.** For each workspace nightshift counts the input and
output tokens, cache reads excluded, of every session that ran for it since
midnight in the daemon's time zone. When the count reaches the workspace's
daily limit, no further session starts for that workspace until the next
midnight or until the person raises the limit with `nightshift workspace
set <slug> --daily-tokens <N>`; sessions that are running finish, and
gating, landing, health commands and publishing go on. The workspace's
thread gets one `Unread` entry, `daily limit reached: <count> of <limit>
tokens`, once per day. Repair sessions start even when the limit is
reached, and are counted.

### Pausing

`nightshift item pause <N>` ends the item's running session, recorded as
interrupted, and holds the item: no session starts for it and it is not
landed or published. Its state is kept and `item show` and `item list` mark
it `paused`. `nightshift item resume <N>` continues it with the step it was
at. `nightshift workspace pause <slug>` and `nightshift workspace resume
<slug>` do the same for every item of the workspace, repairs included, and
for items created while it is paused; `workspace list` marks the workspace
`paused`.

A decision of a paused item can still be answered; the answer takes effect
at the resume. Pausing an item that is `done` or `abandoned`, or one
already paused, exits 1 with the reason; so does resuming one that is not
paused.

### Stopping and restarting

On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` the daemon stops starting sessions, ends the
running ones and records each as interrupted. At the next start, a work
item whose session was interrupted, or was running when the process died,
gets a new session for the same step; the interrupted one does not count
as a failed attempt.

### Status

`GET /api/v1/status` reports the running sessions in `sessions`, each with
`id`, `item`, `workspace`, `role`, `model`, `started_at` and `tokens`, and
the member `isolation`, `user` or `unisolated`. `nightshift status` prints
`sessions: unisolated` when it is so, and one line per running session.
Each workspace's tokens used today are in the `workspaces` member that
package 02 serves, from the count this package keeps.

### The daemon's API and the client

| Command | Route | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `nightshift item pause <N>` | `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/pause` | `200` with the item; prints `paused item <N>` |
| `nightshift item resume <N>` | `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/resume` | `200` with the item; prints `resumed item <N>` |
| `nightshift workspace pause <slug>` | `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/pause` | `200` with the workspace; prints `paused <slug>` |
| `nightshift workspace resume <slug>` | `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/resume` | `200` with the workspace; prints `resumed <slug>` |
| `nightshift session log <session-id>` | `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/log` | `200`, `application/x-ndjson`: the stream as it was written |

A refusal is `409 conflict` with the reason as `message` (`item 12 is
done`, `item 12 is abandoned`, `item 12 is already paused`, `item 12 is
not paused`, `item 12 is paused with its workspace demo`, `workspace demo
is already paused`, `workspace demo is not paused`); an item, a workspace
or a session the daemon does not know, and a session whose stream is no
longer kept, is `404 not_found`.

### What this package offers the later ones

Packages 05 to 10 run nothing themselves; they use these, by these names:

- **`internal/sched`, `Scheduler.RegisterStep(state, StepFunc)`**: the
  function that carries out the step of an item state, `func(ctx, item)
  error`. Its context is cancelled when the item is paused or the daemon
  stops.
- **`Scheduler.RunSession(ctx, Request) (session.Result, error)`**: asks
  for a session and waits for its end. A `Request` is a `session.Spec`
  (`Item`, `Role`, `Step`, `Fork`, `Branch` or `Commit`, `Prompt`,
  `Inputs`, `Accept`) and a `Class`. The result's `Outcome` is
  `completed`, `failed` or `interrupted`; on anything but `completed` the
  step returns and leaves the item as it is. `sched.ErrNotStarted` says
  the limit per item refused the session.
- **`sched.ClassRepair`**: the class of a repair's sessions: first in the
  start order and exempt from the daily limit. Without a class a request
  takes its place from its item's state.
- **`Scheduler.RegisterGuard(name, guard)`** and **`Scheduler.Waiting(item)`**:
  a start guard, and the reason an item's session waits (`a free session`,
  `the hub`, `the daily limit`, or a guard's).
- **`Scheduler.RecordFailure(ctx, item, step, reason, streamPath)`** and
  **`Scheduler.OpenSessionFailed(ctx, item, step, failures)`**: a failure
  of a step that was not a session's, and the `session_failed` decision
  opened directly.
- **`Scheduler.Paused(item)`, `Scheduler.OnPause(fn)`,
  `Scheduler.OnResume(fn)`**.
- **`session.UserRunner`**: runs a command as the session user. It is the
  identity of package 02's `command.Runner` from this package on, so the
  gate and the health command need nothing more.
- **The decision kinds `session_failed`** (`retry`, `abandon`) **and
  `session_limit`** (`continue`, `abandon`), to which package 09 adds
  `take_over`.

### End-to-end flows

**A session from start to its record.** An item is `implementing` and its
step asks for an implementer session. `nightshiftd` registers the session
on the hub, mints a token bound to the item's fork, clones the fork as the
session user and starts `claude -p`. The session writes its stream and a
result file and exits. nightshift reports the usage, completes the session
on the hub, revokes the token and writes the thread entries. The person
runs `nightshift session log <id>` and reads the stream. The item's review
step then runs a reviewer session in a clone of its own and receives the
verdict `agree`.

**A step that fails twice.** The implementer session of item 21 ends with
an error; the step is started once more and fails again. A
`session_failed` decision appears in `nightshift inbox --action` with both
reasons and both stream paths. The person answers `retry`; the step runs
again and completes.

**The daily limit.** Workspace `demo` has used 50,000,000 tokens by 15:00.
Its two running sessions finish; its three `ready` items stay `ready`; an
item whose review had passed still lands and is published. The workspace's
thread says `daily limit reached`. After midnight the three items start.

**A pause and a resume.** The person runs `nightshift item pause 21` while
its implementer runs. The session ends, recorded as interrupted; `item
show 21` marks it `paused` and no session starts for it. The person runs
`nightshift item resume 21`; a new implementer session starts for the same
step, and no `session_failed` decision opens for the interruption.

**A restart in the middle.** `nightshiftd` receives `SIGTERM` while two
implementers run; both sessions are ended and recorded as interrupted, and
the daemon exits with code 0. At the next start both items get a new
session for the same step.

## Design Decisions

From the source PRD, by its numbers:

- **5. The spend limit is one daily token limit per workspace; at the
  limit, running sessions finish and none starts.** The owner decided it.
- **6. Items and workspaces can be paused.** The owner decided it.
- **9. Sessions run on the daemon's machine as an operating-system user of
  their own.** The owner decided it.
- **10. The `sandbox` runner is a later PRD.** The owner decided it.
- **18. Items never wait for each other on files.** The owner decided it.
- **20. The reviewer works in a fresh context, and may run on any provider
  and model, the writer's included.** The owner decided it.
- **21. The implementer runs on `claude -p`, the reviewer on
  `agentkit-go`.** Kept from PRD 01.
- **24. A session's token holds `git:write` only.** Chosen there.
- **25. A session is ended at 10,000,000 tokens.** Chosen there.
- **26. Repairs start although the daily limit is reached.** Chosen there.
- **31. The numbers** (3 parallel sessions, 2 attempts per step, 12
  sessions per item, a 30-minute stall, 10,000,000 tokens per session,
  50,000,000 per workspace and day) are starting values, each configured.
- **36. Every session reports through a result file.** Chosen in PRD 09 of
  `agent-fox-dev/spec`.
- **41. The gate and the health command run as the session user.** Chosen
  there.
- **43. The session limit counts from the person's last answer.** Chosen
  there.

Chosen here:

1. **A process is started as the session user with `sudo -n -H -u <user>
   --`, on Linux and on macOS, also when the daemon is root.** Why: one
   mechanism for both systems, no daemon that must be root, and the
   operating system's own rule (`sudoers`) says who may become whom.
2. **What `sudo` starts is `nightshiftd` itself in a helper mode
   (`nightshiftd session-helper`), which reads one JSON document from its
   standard input (the command, its directory and its environment), runs
   the command in a process group of its own and ends that group when its
   standard input closes.** Why: an unprivileged daemon cannot signal a
   process of another user, so it ends a session by closing a pipe; a
   daemon that dies closes the pipe too, so no session outlives it; and
   secrets travel on standard input, not on a command line another user
   can list. The helper runs in unisolated mode as well, without `sudo`.
3. **A session's process gets only the environment nightshift gives it**
   (`HOME`, `PATH`, `USER`, the git settings and what the role needs),
   never the daemon's own. Why: the daemon's environment may hold
   credentials.
4. **Ending a process is `SIGTERM` to its group, then `SIGKILL` after 10
   seconds.** Why: it fits twice into the 25 seconds package 01 gives a
   shutdown step.
5. **`[sessions].user` wins over `[sessions].unisolated`; in unisolated
   mode the `sessions` check still checks that `claude` runs, as the
   daemon's user.** Why: isolation is the safe reading of a contradictory
   file, and a daemon without `claude` cannot work either way.
6. **The `sessions` check asks its questions in the order of the source
   PRD and reports the first that fails; "can read" is tried by opening
   each of the three files for reading as the session user; "`claude`
   runs" is `claude --version` exiting 0 within 30 seconds.**
7. **The reviewer's provider credential is not checked at start.** The
   `roles` check has the three reasons the source PRD names. The reviewer's
   process is given the daemon's environment variables whose names begin
   with `ANTHROPIC_`, `OPENROUTER_` or `OLLAMA_`, and no others; a missing
   credential fails the review session with `agentkit-go`'s error. Why:
   the source PRD names no reason for it, and the key has to reach the
   session's process in any case.
8. **The reviewer session runs in the helper too, as the session user.**
   Why: the source PRD says sessions run as that user, and the reviewer's
   tools read a clone a session wrote.
9. **The reviewer gets the six file navigation tools and no shell or
   write tool.** Why: a review reads; a reviewer that can run the code it
   reviews is a second implementer.
10. **The reviewer's clone is made for each review session and removed
    when it ends; the item's clone is at `<sessions.dir>/items/<N>/clone`,
    a session's files (inputs, result file) at
    `<sessions.dir>/items/<N>/run/<session-id>/`.** Why: "a clone of its
    own" and "not its working directory"; the result file must be outside
    the working tree (PRD 09 of `agent-fox-dev/spec`).
11. **`[sessions].dir` defaults to `nightshift` in the session user's home
    directory.** Why: the clones belong to that user, and its home is the
    one place it can always write. The daemon reads and removes files
    there through the helper.
12. **The session's token reaches git through the process environment (an
    `http.extraHeader` for the hub's URL given with `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`),
    as package 02 does, and the push option `parley.session=<id>` the same
    way (`push.pushOption`).** Why: nothing is left in the clone when the
    token ends, and every push names its session without the agent having
    to.
13. **A session's token is minted with `expires: 30`, the hub's shortest
    lifetime, and revoked when the session ends; tokens of sessions found
    running at a start are revoked then.** Why: `POST …/tokens` takes
    days, and "expires with the session" needs the revocation.
14. **The reviewer's token is minted with `git:read`, as the source PRD
    says. Parley's subset rule counts exact names, so the worker token
    must hold `git:read` beside `git:write` for that mint to succeed; a
    mint the hub refuses fails the session with the hub's message, like
    any error at a session's start.** Why: the source PRD and package 01
    name the worker token's scopes without `git:read`; this package does
    not change another package's start check, and says in
    `docs/configuration.md` that reviews need the scope. Reported to the
    owner as an open point of package 01.
15. **The hub session's `id` is the UUID nightshift gives the session; the
    session is created on the item's workspace, not on its fork.** Why: a
    chosen id makes the create safe to retry, and the hub links work on a
    fork to a session of its parent.
16. **Usage is reported once, at the session's end, as one usage record
    (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`), with the
    cache-creation tokens on the complete; an interrupted, stalled or
    limited session is completed as `failed` with its reason as
    `error_message`.** Why: the source PRD says "when the session ends"
    and "completed or failed".
17. **Reports the hub did not take (unreachable, token not accepted) are
    kept in the store and sent again at each scheduler pass; they never
    hold an item back; `409 session_not_active` ends the tries.**
18. **"Input and output tokens, cache reads excluded" counts input tokens,
    cache-creation tokens and output tokens.** Why: a cache write is
    input that was not read from the cache. For `claude -p` the running
    count is summed over the stream's `assistant` events, one per message
    id, and the `usage` of the last `result` event replaces it when it is
    greater; for the reviewer it is `core.Usage` (`InputTokens +
    CacheWriteTokens + OutputTokens`).
19. **A workspace's daily count grows as usage is observed, at the time it
    is observed, so a running session counts and a session that crosses
    midnight is split between the two days.** Why: the flow "has used
    50,000,000 tokens by 15:00" counts sessions still running.
20. **The `Unread` entry is written when the count first reaches the limit
    on a day, and not again that day, also when the limit was raised and
    reached again.** Why: "once per day".
21. **The start order has a fourth class: a session asked for an item in
    any other state (planning among them) comes after the `ready` items,
    oldest item first.** Why: the source PRD orders three classes and
    planner sessions are in none of them; work in progress goes first.
22. **A session is asked for by an item's step and waits for its turn; the
    scheduler looks at the queue once a second and whenever something
    changed.** Why: a step such as "implement, then gate" is one function,
    and only its session takes one of the parallel places.
23. **The `session_limit` decision opens when a further implementer or
    reviewer session is asked for with the count at the limit.** Why: "no
    further session starts" is what the limit is for; an item whose last
    allowed session finished the work goes on without asking.
24. **Failures are counted per item and step, a step being the name the
    asking package gives (`plan`, `implement`, `review`); a completed
    session of that step, or an answer `retry`, sets the count to zero; an
    interrupted session changes nothing.** A package can also record a
    failure that was not a session's (package 06: a failed gate).
25. **A session that cannot be started (the hub refuses the registration
    or the token, the clone fails) counts as failed with that error's
    first line.** Why: it is "an error", and two of them should reach the
    person as any other failure does.
26. **`retry` is the recommended option of `session_failed`, `continue`
    of `session_limit`.**
27. **Pausing is two flags, one on the item and one on the workspace; an
    item is held while either is set. `item resume` for an item held only
    by its workspace is refused (`item <N> is paused with its workspace
    <slug>`).** Why: `workspace resume` must not release an item the
    person paused by itself.
28. **A pause cancels the item's running step, not only its session.**
    Why: "it is not landed or published"; the step is called again at the
    resume.
29. **The routes** of the table under *The daemon's API and the client*.
    Why: the client speaks only the daemon's API, and the source PRD names
    the commands alone.
30. **`nightshift session log` prints the stream's lines unchanged, with
    and without `--json`.** Why: the stream is JSON lines already.
31. **Streams are files, `<directory of store.path>/streams/<session-id>.jsonl`,
    with the session's standard error beside them as `.stderr`; files of
    sessions that ended more than 30 days ago are removed at start and
    once a day.**
32. **`status` gets the member `isolation`.** Why: `sessions` is a list in
    package 01's document, and `sessions: unisolated` needs a place in the
    JSON.
33. **Thread entries of kind `session_started` and `session_ended`** (role,
    session id, and at the end the outcome, the reason and the tokens);
    neither marks the thread unread.
34. **Events: `session.started` and `session.ended`, and `item.updated`
    and `workspace.updated` for a pause and a resume.**
35. **The item's clone follows the fork's branch and keeps everything
    else.** At a session's start the branch is created at the tip of the
    fork's default branch when neither side has it, set to the fork's head
    when the fork's branch has commits the local one lacks, and left as it
    is otherwise; untracked files are never removed. Why: the fork is what
    the hub and the person see (a person may push to it), and "kept between
    the sessions" is for what a session left behind.
36. **With a session user configured and `clones_dir` (package 02) not
    set, the workspace clones go to `<sessions.dir>/workspaces`.** Why:
    from this package on git, the gate and the health command run as the
    session user, who cannot write in the daemon's home directory.

## Glossary

- **session**: one run of an agent for one step of a work item, as a
  process on the daemon's machine.
- **role**: `planner`, `implementer` or `reviewer`; each has a model, the
  reviewer a provider too.
- **session user**: the operating-system user that sessions, the gate and
  the health command run as.
- **helper**: `nightshiftd` started in the mode that runs one command as
  the session user and ends it when its standard input closes.
- **step**: what an item's state calls for next; a package registers the
  function that carries it out, and names the step of each session it
  asks for.
- **start guard**: a function a package registers that can refuse a
  session's start for an item, with a reason.
- **stream**: everything a session wrote to its standard output, kept as
  a file.
- **result file**: the JSON document a planner or implementer session
  writes at the path it was given.
- **verdict**: a reviewer's `agree` or `object`, with findings.
- **daily limit**: the tokens a workspace's sessions may use between two
  midnights before no further session starts.
- **interrupted**: a session ended by a pause, an abandon, a shutdown or
  the daemon's death; it is not a failure.
- **paused**: an item, or every item of a workspace, held by the person
  until they resume it.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Roles, the session user and running as it

**Rationale:** A session runs without permission prompts, so what it can reach has to be settled by the operating system before the first one starts.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] IF the configuration gives no value for `roles.planner.model`, `roles.implementer.model` or `roles.reviewer.model`, gives none for `roles.reviewer.provider`, or gives a `roles.reviewer.provider` that, trimmed and compared without regard to case, is none of the providers `agentkit-go` lists, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `roles`, which runs after `credentials`, and start nothing
   → exit code 1; exactly one line on stderr, the first that applies of `roles: planner names no model`, `roles: implementer names no model`, `roles: reviewer names no model`, `roles: reviewer names no provider`, `roles: unknown provider "<name>"`; the `sessions` check did not run; no listener is opened and no store file is created
   Check: unit
   ```
   new file internal/session/roles_test.go, a table over {planner model empty, implementer model empty, reviewer model empty, reviewer provider empty, provider 'acme' -> 'unknown provider "acme"', two faults at once -> the first in the order, provider ' Anthropic ' with every model set -> nil, provider 'ollama' -> nil}: err = session.CheckRoles(cfg.Roles); assert err text == want. In internal/daemon/start_test.go (package 01's file): code, stderr = daemon.Run(config whose reviewer has no model, against a fake hub that passes the first three checks); assert code == 1; assert stderr == 'roles: reviewer names no model\n'; assert no store file
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF the configuration gives `sessions.max_parallel` a value outside 1 to 16, `items.max_sessions` a value outside 2 to 100, or `sessions.stall`, `sessions.max_tokens` or `limits.daily_tokens` a value that is not greater than zero, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `config`, and take for each of these keys the file omits its default: 3, 12, 30 minutes, 10,000,000 and 50,000,000
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr: `config: sessions.max_parallel must be between 1 and 16`, `config: items.max_sessions must be between 2 and 100` or `config: <dotted key> must be greater than 0`; a file without the keys loads with the five defaults and `sessions.unisolated` false
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/config_test.go (package 01's file), a table over {max_parallel 0 and 17 -> refused, 1 and 16 -> loaded; max_sessions 1 and 101 -> refused, 2 and 100 -> loaded; stall '0s', max_tokens 0, daily_tokens -1 -> '<key> must be greater than 0'; none of the keys -> 3, 12, 30m, 10000000, 50000000}: cfg, err = config.Load(path, home); assert err text or the values
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF the configuration has neither `sessions.user` nor `sessions.unisolated = true`, or names a `sessions.user` that does not exist on the machine, or names the user nightshiftd itself runs as, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `sessions`, which runs after `roles`, without starting any process
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr: `sessions: no user configured; set [sessions].user or [sessions].unisolated`, `sessions: user "<name>" does not exist` or `sessions: user "<name>" is the daemon's user`; no process was started as another user; a configuration with both a user and `unisolated = true` is checked as one with the user alone
   Check: unit
   - setup: the check's 30 second timeout for `claude --version` is a parameter, set to 50 milliseconds for the timeout row
   ```
   new file internal/session/usercheck_test.go, one table for every way the sessions check fails, over a stub user lookup and a stub of the run-as function that records what it is asked to run; these rows: {no user and unisolated false, user 'ghost' unknown to the lookup, user equal to the current user}: err = session.CheckUser(ctx, cfg, deps); assert err text == want; assert the stub ran nothing. Rows for the next criterion: {the probe fails with 'sudo: a password is required' -> 'cannot run as "agent": sudo: a password is required', the store file opens for reading as the user -> 'user "agent" can read <store path>', config and token both readable -> the config path is named, 'claude --version' exits 127 -> 'claude is not available to "agent": <first line of its error output>', claude does not answer within the timeout parameter -> the same reason with 'timeout'}; a last row where everything holds -> nil
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF the configured session user exists and is not the daemon's, and a probe process cannot be started as that user, or the configuration file, the client token file or the store file can be opened for reading by a process running as that user, or `claude --version` run as that user does not exit 0 within 30 seconds, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `sessions`, asking in that order and naming the first that fails, with the files in the order configuration, token, store
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr: `sessions: cannot run as "<name>": <first line of the error>`, `sessions: user "<name>" can read <path>` or `sessions: claude is not available to "<name>": <first line of the error>`; a file that does not exist yet, as the token file and the store file at a first start, counts as not readable
   Check: same as REQ-1.3
1. [REQ-1.5] WHEN nightshiftd starts with `sessions.unisolated = true` and no `sessions.user`, THE nightshiftd SHALL pass the `sessions` check when `claude --version` exits 0 as the daemon's user, print one warning line to stderr, and run every session and every command of `internal/command` as the daemon's user
   → stderr holds `warning: sessions run as the daemon's user and can read its credentials` exactly once; `GET /api/v1/status` answers `"isolation": "unisolated"`, and `"isolation": "user"` with no warning line when a session user is configured; without a working `claude` the start fails with exit code 1 and `sessions: claude is not available to "<daemon's user>": <error>`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake hub that passes the first three checks
   - setup: a fake `claude` (a script the test writes) that prints a version and exits 0

   in internal/daemon/start_test.go, a table over {unisolated with a fake claude on PATH -> the daemon runs, stderr has the warning line once, status.isolation == 'unisolated'; unisolated with no claude on PATH -> code 1 and stderr starts with 'sessions: claude is not available to "'}; the isolated case uses a run-as function injected into daemon.Run that starts the helper directly: assert status.isolation == 'user' and no warning line
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] THE nightshiftd SHALL for any process of a session and any command `internal/command` runs, start it as the session user by running `sudo -n -H -u <user> -- <the nightshiftd executable> session-helper`, or the helper alone when sessions are unisolated, and have the helper run the command in the directory given with an environment that holds `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME` and `PATH` as the helper has them, the variables given with the command, and no other variable of the daemon
   → the command's output and exit code reach the caller; a variable set in the daemon's environment and not given with the command is absent from the command's environment; the command, its directory and its variables are sent to the helper on its standard input and appear in no argument list
   Check: integration
   - setup: the helper is the test binary, re-executed through a TestMain that calls the helper's entry function when the first argument is `session-helper`
   - setup: no `sudo` is run by any test
   ```
   new file internal/session/runas_test.go: assert session.HelperArgv('agent', exe) == ['sudo','-n','-H','-u','agent','--',exe,'session-helper'] and session.HelperArgv('', exe) == [exe,'session-helper']. With the test binary re-executed as the helper and NIGHTSHIFT_TEST_SECRET=x set in the test's environment: res = runner.Run(ctx, {argv: ['sh','-c','pwd; env'], dir: tmp, env: {A: '1'}}); assert the first output line == tmp; assert output has 'A=1' and 'HOME='; assert output lacks 'NIGHTSHIFT_TEST_SECRET'; assert res.ExitCode == 0; a command 'exit 3' -> ExitCode 3. In internal/daemon/start_test.go: after a start, a command run through internal/command went through the injected run-as function
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] WHEN nightshiftd ends a process it started through the helper, or the helper's standard input closes because nightshiftd's own process ended, THE nightshiftd SHALL send SIGTERM to every process of the command's process group, send SIGKILL 10 seconds later to those that remain, and end the helper
   → no process of the group remains once the helper has ended; the caller's wait returns with the outcome `ended` and not with an exit code; a command that ignores SIGTERM is gone after the 10 seconds, which are a parameter
   Check: integration
   - setup: the grace between SIGTERM and SIGKILL set to 200 milliseconds
   ```
   in internal/session/runas_test.go, a table over {the caller cancels its context, the caller's end of the helper's standard input is closed as a dying daemon would} x {command 'sleep 600 & sleep 600 & wait' that writes its children's pids first, command with `trap '' TERM` in front}: start; read the pids; end; assert the wait returns within grace + 1s with outcome ended; assert kill(pid, 0) fails for every pid
   ```

### REQ-2: A session, its token, its hub record and its stream

**Rationale:** A session is the unit that costs tokens and writes code, so each one is registered, confined to its item's fork and kept readable afterwards.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a session is started for an item, THE nightshiftd SHALL give the session a UUID, create a session on the hub with the worker token (`POST /api/v1/sessions` with `id` that UUID, `workspace_slug` the item's workspace, `archetype` the role, `model` the role's model, `metadata` `{"item": <number>}`), mint a token bound to the item's fork (`POST /api/v1/workspaces/{fork}/tokens` with `permissions` `["git:write"]` for a planner or an implementer and `["git:read"]` for a reviewer, and `expires` 30), record the session as `running` in the store, and write a `session_started` entry with the role and the session id to the item's thread
   → the hub holds an `active` session with that id, archetype, model and metadata; the minted token is bound to the fork and holds exactly the one scope; the token's value is in no file, no store row and no log line; the event `session.started` is appended
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) extended with the session routes, the workspace token route and the token revocation, holding the workspace `demo` and its fork `demo--i7` with a git endpoint
   - setup: an item 7 of `demo` created through internal/item
   - setup: sessions unisolated, the helper being the re-executed test binary
   - setup: a fake `claude` on PATH and, for the reviewer, a provider/faux client
   ```
   new file internal/session/session_test.go, a table over the roles {planner, implementer, reviewer}: res = svc.Run(ctx, spec); assert fakeHub.Session(res.ID) == {workspace_slug: 'demo', archetype: role, model: cfg model of the role, metadata: {item: 7}}; assert the token minted for the fork has permissions == ['git:write'] (reviewer: ['git:read']) and expires 30; assert the store file, the stream and the daemon's log do not contain the token's value; assert the item's thread has a session_started entry
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN a planner or implementer session starts, THE nightshiftd SHALL bring the clone at `<sessions.dir>/items/<N>/clone` to the given branch of the item's fork as the session user (cloning the fork when the clone does not exist and fetching otherwise; creating the branch at the tip of the fork's default branch when neither side has it; setting the local branch to the fork's head when it does not contain that head; and leaving it as it is otherwise), write the session's input files to `<sessions.dir>/items/<N>/run/<session-id>/`, and run `claude -p <prompt> --model <the role's model> --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions --disallowedTools ScheduleWakeup,CronCreate` in the clone, with `{result}` in the prompt replaced by the path `result.json` in that run directory and each `{input:<name>}` by the path of that input file, and with an environment in which git sends the session's token to the hub's URL, every push carries the option `parley.session=<session id>`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` is the stall time in milliseconds
   → `claude` received exactly those arguments with the clone as its working directory; a `git push` it ran reached the hub authenticated with the session's token and carrying the push option; a file a first session left untracked in the clone, and a commit it did not push, are there for the item's second session; a local branch the fork's branch has moved away from is at the fork's head when the next session starts; the clone's `.git/config` holds neither the token nor an `extraheader`; a prompt naming an input that was not given fails the start with `unknown input "<name>"`
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/session/session_test.go: the fake claude records its arguments and working directory, reads the file named after '--findings' in its prompt, creates 'left.txt', commits and pushes a branch, and writes the result file. svc.Run(spec{Role: implementer, Branch: 'item-7', Prompt: 'af-impl x --rework {input:findings} --result {result}', Inputs: {findings: '[]'}}); assert the recorded argv == ['-p', <prompt with both paths>, '--model', 'm-impl', '--output-format', 'stream-json', '--verbose', '--permission-mode', 'bypassPermissions', '--disallowedTools', 'ScheduleWakeup,CronCreate']; assert cwd == <dir>/items/7/clone and its checked-out branch == 'item-7'; assert fakeHub saw a push to demo--i7 bearing the session's token with option 'parley.session=' + res.ID; run a second session; assert its claude saw left.txt; push another commit to the fork's item-7 from outside and add an unpushed local commit; run a third session; assert its HEAD == the fork's head; assert read(clone/.git/config) contains neither the token nor 'extraheader'; a spec whose prompt names {input:nope} -> outcome failed, reason 'unknown input "nope"'
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN a reviewer session starts, THE nightshiftd SHALL make a clone of the item's fork at the given commit, detached, in a directory of that session alone, run as the session user an `agentkit-go` agent built with the provider and the model of `[roles.reviewer]`, the six file navigation tools over that clone and no other tool, no earlier message, and the prompt as its one user message, write each event of the run as one JSON line to the session's output, and remove that clone when the session ends
   → the provider's first request holds the prompt as its only user message and no message of any other session; the tools offered are exactly those `tools.FileNavigationTools()` names; a `read_file` call returns the file as it is at the commit; after the session its clone directory does not exist and the item's own clone is unchanged; a second review of the same item again starts with the prompt alone
   Check: integration
   - setup: the helper's entry function takes the provider client as an option; the test's helper passes a provider/faux client scripted from a file the test writes
   ```
   in internal/session/session_test.go: the faux provider is scripted with faux.ToolCall('1', 'read_file', {path: 'README.md'}) and then faux.Text('{"verdict":"agree","findings":[]}'). res = svc.Run(spec{Role: reviewer, Commit: <commit>, Prompt: 'review this'}); reqs = faux.Requests(); assert the user messages of reqs[0] == ['review this']; assert the tool names of reqs[0] == tools.FileNavigationTools(); assert the tool result in reqs[1] holds README.md's content at the commit; assert res.Verdict.Verdict == 'agree'; assert the session's review directory is gone; run a second review with another prompt; assert its first request holds that prompt alone
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN a session's process ends, and for a planner or implementer the last `result` event of its stream does not say `is_error` and `result.json` in its run directory holds one JSON document, or for a reviewer the last message holds one JSON object whose `verdict` is `agree`, or `object` with at least one finding that has a `text`, and the accept function given with the session returns no error, THE nightshiftd SHALL record the session as `completed` and return to the caller its id, the outcome, its tokens, the path of its stream, and the result file's document or the verdict with its findings (`text`, and `file`, `line` and `criterion` where given)
   → the caller receives the outcome `completed` and a nil error; the result file's bytes are returned as written; the verdict object is taken from the first `{` to the last `}` of the last message, so text around it does not matter; the accept function was called once, after the process ended, with that result
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/session/session_test.go, a table over {implementer whose fake claude writes result.json {"outcome":"written"} and a last result event with is_error false -> res.Outcome == completed, res.ResultFile == those bytes; reviewer whose last message is 'Here: {"verdict":"object","findings":[{"text":"t","file":"a.go","line":3}]} done' -> res.Verdict == {object, [{t, a.go, 3}]}}: assert err == nil; assert res.StreamPath names an existing file; assert the accept function saw the same result once
   ```
1. ### REQ-3: Bounds on a session, failed steps and the limit per item

**Rationale:** Nobody watches a session, so it must end by itself, and a step that keeps failing must reach the person instead of spending the day's tokens.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] IF a running session writes no line to its standard output or its standard error for `sessions.stall`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL end the session's process group and record the session as `failed`
   → the caller receives the outcome `failed` with the reason `stalled`; no process of the session remains; the hub's session is completed as `failed` with `error_message` `stalled`; a session that writes one line just before each stall time elapses is not ended
   Check: integration
   - setup: `sessions.stall` set to 100 milliseconds and `sessions.max_tokens` to 1000 for this test
   - setup: the fake claude sleeps on request
   ```
   new file internal/session/limits_test.go, one table for the two bounds; these rows: {fake claude prints one line and sleeps -> failed, 'stalled'; fake claude prints a line every 20ms for 200ms and then its result -> completed}; rows for the next criterion: {assistant events reporting input 600 + cache creation 300 + output 100 with max_tokens 1000 -> failed, 'token limit'; assistant events reporting cache read 5000 and input 10 -> completed; the same message id reported in two events with input 600 -> counted once, completed; reviewer whose faux turns carry Usage{InputTokens: 700, CacheWriteTokens: 200, OutputTokens: 100} -> failed, 'token limit'}: res = svc.Run(ctx, spec); assert res.Outcome and res.Reason; assert the session's process is gone; assert fakeHub.Session(res.ID).error_message == res.Reason
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF the input tokens, cache-creation tokens and output tokens a running session has reported in its stream, cache-read tokens not counted, reach `sessions.max_tokens`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL end the session's process group and record the session as `failed`
   → the caller receives the outcome `failed` with the reason `token limit`; the session's tokens are the count at which it was ended; a planner's or implementer's count sums the `usage` of the stream's `assistant` events, each message id once, and a reviewer's the usage its agent reports after each turn
   Check: same as REQ-3.1
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN a session asked for an item and a step ends `failed`, or a package records a failure for that item and step, and it is the first failure in a row for that item and step, THE nightshiftd SHALL open no decision, and let the scheduler call the item's step function again, so that the step is started once more
   → no decision is open for the item; its step function is called again at the next pass; a session of that step that ends `completed` sets the item's count of failures in a row for the step to zero; a failure of another step of the item does not add to it
   Check: unit
   ```
   new file internal/sched/failures_test.go, with a fake session runner whose outcomes the test scripts and a real inbox and item store: script {failed 'a', completed, failed 'b', failed 'c'} for step 'implement'; let the scheduler run its passes; assert no decision after the first and the third session; assert the step function was called four times; assert one session_failed decision after the fourth whose evidence names 'b' and 'c', not 'a'. Second case: failed for step 'implement' then failed for step 'review' -> no decision. Third case: sched.RecordFailure(item, 'implement', 'gate failed', '') after one failed session -> the decision opens
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a session ends `failed`, or a package records a failure, and it is the second failure in a row for that item and step, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL open a decision of kind `session_failed` on the item's thread with the options `retry`, recommended, and `abandon`, whose evidence holds both reasons and the path of each session's stream, and start no further session for the item while the decision is open
   → `GET /api/v1/decisions` lists the decision with exactly the option keys `retry` and `abandon` and with both reasons and both stream paths in its evidence; the item's `waiting_on` names it; the item keeps its state; its step function is not called while the decision is open
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/sched/failures_test.go: after two failed sessions ('boom' and 'stalled'): d = the open decision of the item; assert d.kind == 'session_failed'; assert d.options keys == ['retry','abandon'] and the recommended one is 'retry'; assert d.evidence holds 'boom', 'stalled' and both sessions' stream paths; assert item.waiting_on.id == d.id; run three more passes; assert the step function's call count did not change
   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] WHEN a `session_failed` decision is answered `retry`, or a `session_limit` decision is answered `continue`, THE nightshiftd SHALL for `retry`, set the count of failures in a row of the decision's step to zero; for `continue`, count the item's sessions from the time of the answer; and call the item's step function again
   → after `retry` the step's next session starts within one pass, and two further failures in a row open a new `session_failed` decision; after `continue` up to `items.max_sessions` further implementer and reviewer sessions start before a new `session_limit` decision opens; a handler called twice for one answer has the effect of one call
   Check: integration
   ```
   new file internal/sched/decisions_test.go, a table over the two kinds and their options through POST /api/v1/decisions/{id}/answer; these rows: {session_failed + retry -> the step function is called again, a third and fourth failed session open a second decision; session_limit + continue with max_sessions 2 -> two further sessions start and the third request opens a second decision}; rows for the abandon criterion: {session_failed + abandon, session_limit + abandon -> item.state == 'abandoned', the item's directory is gone, no further step call}; each handler is then invoked a second time directly and the assertions repeated
   ```
1. [REQ-3.6] IF an implementer or reviewer session is asked for an item, and the number of implementer and reviewer sessions started for that item since the later of the time it became `ready` and the time of the last answer to a decision of that item has reached `items.max_sessions`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL start no session, tell the asking step that none was started, and open a decision of kind `session_limit` on the item's thread with the options `continue`, recommended, and `abandon`, whose evidence lists each counted session with its role, its outcome and its tokens
   → the asking step receives the error `sched.ErrNotStarted`; exactly one `session_limit` decision is open for the item however often the step asks; its option keys are `continue` and `abandon`; planner sessions are neither counted nor refused; a session that ended `interrupted` is counted, since it was started; an answer to any decision of the item starts the count again
   Check: unit
   ```

   ```
1. [REQ-3.7] WHEN a `session_failed` or `session_limit` decision is answered `abandon`, THE nightshiftd SHALL abandon the item through the abandon function of `internal/item`, which calls the abandon hooks
   → the item's state is `abandoned`; no step function is called for it afterwards
   Check: same as REQ-3.5
1. [REQ-3.8] WHEN an item becomes `done` or `abandoned`, THE nightshiftd SHALL end the item's running sessions, recording each as `interrupted`, and remove the directory `<sessions.dir>/items/<N>` with the item's clone and its run directories
   → the directory does not exist; no process of a session of the item remains; the streams of the item's sessions are still served by `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/log`; the removal of an item that never had a session succeeds; the abandon hook registered with `internal/item` returns after the sessions ended

### REQ-4: The scheduler and the daily limit

**Rationale:** Items are independent, so they should run at once; tokens are money, so a workspace must stop spending at a known point.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] THE nightshiftd SHALL for any item whose state has a registered step function, that is not paused, has no open decision and has no step running, call that function with the item in a goroutine of its own, at each pass, a pass being run once a second and whenever an item, a decision or a session changed
   → at most one step function runs for an item at a time; a function that returns without changing the item is called again at the next pass; a function that returns an error or panics is written to the daemon's log with the item's number and called again at the next pass, and the daemon keeps running; an item in a state without a function is left alone; a slow step of one item does not delay another item's step
   Check: unit
   ```
   new file internal/sched/sched_test.go, with the pass triggered by the test instead of the one second timer: register a step for 'implementing' that counts its calls and blocks on a channel; items 1 and 2 implementing, item 3 in 'landing' with no function, item 4 implementing with an open decision; pass twice; assert calls == {1: 1, 2: 1} and none for 3 and 4; release item 1; pass; assert calls[1] == 2 while item 2 is still in its first call. A step that panics for item 5: assert the log line names item 5, the next pass calls it again, and items 1 and 2 are still served
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] THE nightshiftd SHALL run at most `sessions.max_parallel` sessions at once over all workspaces, a session asked for beyond that waiting until a running one has ended
   → with `max_parallel` 2 and five sessions asked for, never more than two run at the same moment and all five run; a waiting request whose context is cancelled returns that context's error and takes no place
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sched/sched_test.go, with a fake session runner that records the number running at once and ends each session when the test says: ask for five sessions from five step functions with max_parallel 2; assert max concurrent == 2; end them one by one; assert five ran. Cancel the context of a sixth waiting request; assert it returns context.Canceled and the runner never saw it
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN a place becomes free while several asked sessions wait, THE nightshiftd SHALL start the waiting sessions in this order: those asked with the repair class; then those of items in `implementing` or `reviewing`, by the time each was asked; then those of items in `ready`, by the time each item became `ready`, oldest first; then those of items in any other state, by the item's creation time, oldest first
   → the order in which the sessions start is the order given, whatever the order in which they were asked
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sched/sched_test.go, with max_parallel 1 and one session running: ask, in this order, for {item A in 'new' created at T1, item B ready since T5, item C ready since T3, item D reviewing asked at T9, item E implementing asked at T8, item F asked with sched.ClassRepair, item G in 'planning' created at T0}; end sessions one at a time; assert the start order == [F, E, D, C, B, G, A]
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] WHILE a registered start guard refuses an item, THE nightshiftd SHALL start no session for that item, start the waiting sessions of other items in their order, report the guard's reason as what the item waits for, and ask the guard again at each pass
   → the refused request keeps waiting and does not take a place; `Scheduler.Waiting(item)` returns the reason of the first refusing guard in registration order; once the guard allows the item its session starts at the next free place; a guard that returns an error is treated as refusing, with the error's first line as the reason
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/sched/sched_test.go: sched.RegisterGuard('dependency', g) where g refuses item B with 'waits for package 03' until a flag is set; ask for sessions of B (ready since T1) and C (ready since T2) with max_parallel 1; assert C starts and B does not; assert sched.Waiting(B) == 'waits for package 03'; set the flag; end C; assert B starts; assert the guard was asked at each pass
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] WHILE the hub is unreachable or does not accept the worker token (`Available` of the hub client is false for the worker credential), THE nightshiftd SHALL start no session, let the sessions that run go on, and start the waiting ones in their order once the hub is available again
   → no request for a session reaches the hub while it is unavailable; a session that was running ends with its own outcome; `Scheduler.Waiting(item)` returns `the hub`; the waiting sessions start without a restart of the daemon
   Check: unit

   ```
1. [REQ-4.6] THE nightshiftd SHALL for any workspace, add the input tokens, cache-creation tokens and output tokens its items' sessions report, cache-read tokens not counted, to a count kept in the store for the day, in the daemon's time zone, on which each report is observed, and give the count of the current day as the workspace's tokens used today
   → `GET /api/v1/status` and `nightshift workspace show` report the count of the current day through the source package 02 offers; tokens a session reports before local midnight count for that day and those it reports after for the next; the count survives a restart; the tokens of a repair session are counted; the count holds a running session's tokens so far

   → a session asked for an item of another workspace starts; a step function of the workspace that asks for no session is still called; `Scheduler.Waiting(item)` returns `the daily limit`; the waiting sessions start in their order, without a restart, at the first pass after local midnight or after the limit was set above the count; a repair-class session starts although the limit is reached

Then a table over {clock moved past local midnight, limit raised to 2000}: pass; assert the waiting session starts

   → the workspace's thread holds exactly one such entry per local day, also when further tokens are counted, when the limit was raised and reached again on that day, and when the daemon was restarted in between; on the next day the limit being reached writes one again

### REQ-5: Pausing and resuming

**Rationale:** A person who sees something going wrong must be able to stop it at once, and to let it go on later from where it was.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/pause` names an item that is neither `done` nor `abandoned` and that no pause flag holds, neither its own nor its workspace's, THE nightshiftd SHALL set the item's pause flag, cancel its running step, end its running session and record that session as `interrupted`, keep the item's state, and append the event `item.updated`
   → status 200 with the item, whose `markers` hold `paused`; `nightshift item pause <N>` prints `paused item <N>` and exits 0, and with `--json` prints the item; the session's outcome is `interrupted`; the functions registered with `OnPause` were each called once with the item
   Check: integration

In internal/cli/cli_test.go: ['item','pause','7'] -> code 0, stdout 'paused item 7\n'
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHILE an item's pause flag is set, or the pause flag of its workspace is set, THE nightshiftd SHALL call no step function for the item, start no session for it, also not one asked with the repair class, keep its state, and report the marker `paused` for it
   → `nightshift item show <N>` and `nightshift item list` print `paused` for the item; `Scheduler.Paused(item)` is true; an item created in a paused workspace is held from its creation; the pause flags survive a restart
   Check: unit

   in internal/sched/pause_test.go: pause item 7; pass three times; assert its step function was not called and a ClassRepair request for it does not start; assert sched.Paused(7); pause workspace 'demo', create item 9 in it; pass; assert no step call for 9 and its markers hold 'paused'; reopen the store; assert both flags are still set

[REQ-5.3] WHEN `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/resume` names an item whose pause flag is set, THE nightshiftd SHALL clear the flag, append the event `item.updated`, call the functions registered with `OnResume`, and, unless the item's workspace is paused, call the item's step function for its state at the next pass
   → status 200 with the item, whose `markers` no longer hold `paused`; `nightshift item resume <N>` prints `resumed item <N>` and exits 0; a new session for the step the interrupted one was for starts; no `session_failed` decision is opened for the interruption

   → status 200 with the workspace, whose `paused` is `true` after a pause and `false` after a resume; `nightshift workspace pause <slug>` prints `paused <slug>` and `resume` prints `resumed <slug>`; `nightshift workspace list` prints `paused` after the workspace's state; an item paused by itself before the workspace's pause stays paused after the workspace's resume

   → status 409 with `error_type` `conflict` and the message `item <N> is done`, `item <N> is abandoned`, `item <N> is already paused`, `item <N> is not paused`, `item <N> is paused with its workspace <slug>`, `workspace <slug> is already paused` or `workspace <slug> is not paused`; status 404 `not_found` for an unknown item or workspace; the `nightshift` command exits 1 with the message on stderr; no flag changed and no event was appended; a command without its argument, or with a number that is no positive integer, exits 2

   → the answer route answers as for any decision; until the resume an item answered `abandon` is not `abandoned` and an item answered `retry` or `continue` starts no session; at the resume `abandon` leaves the item `abandoned`, and `retry` or `continue` lets its step start; an answer given before a restart of the daemon is still carried out at the resume after it
